prompt: A computer monitor uses pixels composed of red, green, and blue elements. Is this related more to the physics of light or to human physiology? Please explain. If normal humans all had red-green colorblindness how many color elements would most computer monitors use for each pixel?
response: The composition of pixels into red, green, and blue elements is primarily a result of human physiology, specifically how our eyes perceive color. If normal humans all had red-green colorblindness, computer monitors would likely use only one color element per pixel to simplify display technology.
